name: zyvor-fluxvm
description: FluxVM is a Rust-native virtualization platform for running and managing virtual machines across Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, QEMU/KVM, Apple Virtualization.framework, and FluxVM’s own in-tree hypervisor.  One API. One CLI. Multiple hypervisors.  FluxVM removes the traditional libvirt/XML stack and replaces it with a modern, programmable architec

paragraphs: Primary networking: native eBPF. VM edges require successful attachment by default; nftables is an explicit compatibility mode. Before upgrading configs that omit the dataplane mode, follow the eBPF upgrade guide.

One Rust control plane for Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, QEMU/KVM and the in-tree FluxVM hypervisor, plus Apple's Virtualization.framework (vz) on a Mac. No libvirtd. No XML. A REST API and a CLI that do the same thing on every backend, with a vsock guest agent instead of SSH.
4 Linux backends + vz on Mac, one API · No libvirtd, no XML · Native KVM, no QEMU · SDKs: Python, Go, TypeScript · Operator verified on real k3s
features: CI runners that isolate every job: a VM per job over vsock exec, with ttlseconds cleanup.
AI-agent sandboxes with guard rails: a microVM or a rootless procbox, an egress ACL and a change-set.
Linux VMs with no QEMU installed: the in-tree KVM engine and a golden template, fluxctl vm-template create native-agent .
A golden-image pipeline: build once with fluxctl build-image, reuse through CoW overlays and a signed catalog.
Kubernetes-native VMs without KubeVirt and OCI workloads with a per-Pod guest kernel.
